content.value_statement: Important architecture choices often lose their rationale over time. This skill provides structured ADR templates, examples, and review guidance for preserving decisions and trade-offs.
actual_capabilities: Structures ADRs with status, context, decision, consequences, alternatives, and references.
Provides reusable Markdown and YAML templates for consistent records.
Supplies complete examples for microservices, PostgreSQL, and API versioning decisions.
Reviews ADR quality with technical, business, operational, compliance, and stakeholder criteria.
Guides ADR lifecycle management from proposal through acceptance, implementation, and supersession.
limitations: It does not validate architecture choices against a live codebase or infrastructure.
It does not approve decisions or replace stakeholder review.
Its examples require adaptation to current project constraints, costs, and technology versions.
It does not automatically create files, update indexes, or enforce ADR status changes.

use_cases.title: Record a technology choice
use_cases.description: Create a clear ADR that compares options and preserves the reasons behind a selected database, framework, or platform.

use_cases.title: Review a proposed decision
use_cases.description: Assess an ADR for missing context, weak alternatives, hidden consequences, and incomplete approvals before acceptance.

use_cases.title: Build project decision history
use_cases.description: Standardize ADR structure and lifecycle practices so future contributors can understand how the system evolved.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ADR for choosing [technology] for [project]. Include status, context, decision, consequences, two alternatives, and references. Ask for missing facts before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a first ADR for a straightforward technology decision.

prompt_templates.title: Review an ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ADR using the included checklist: [paste ADR]. Identify missing context, weak alternatives, unclear consequences, and required stakeholder approvals. Return prioritized revisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineering lead needs structured feedback before accepting a proposal.

prompt_templates.title: Compare constrained options
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR for [decision] under these constraints: [constraints]. Compare [option A], [option B], and [option C] using measurable criteria. State assumptions and unresolved risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: An architect must explain a complex choice with several credible alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Supersede an accepted ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new ADR that supersedes [ADR number]. Preserve the original decision history, explain changed conditions, assess migration consequences, and link both records.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs to replace an accepted decision without rewriting historical records.

output_examples.input: Document why the payments service should use PostgreSQL instead of MySQL or DynamoDB.
output: Context: The service requires relational integrity, complex reporting, and managed operations.
Decision: Use PostgreSQL on a managed service.
Consequences: Strong SQL support and portability, with migration and operational costs.
Alternatives: MySQL and DynamoDB, compared against query, consistency, and portability needs.

output_examples.input: Review our proposed API versioning ADR before the architecture meeting.
output: Priority revision: Define measurable compatibility and deprecation requirements.
Missing consequence: Explain monitoring, documentation, and client migration costs.
Alternative gap: Compare URL paths with headers and query parameters.
Approval gap: Identify API owners, security reviewers, and affected client teams.

output_examples.input: Replace ADR-0004 because its deployment assumptions have changed.
output_examples.output: A new proposed ADR references ADR-0004, explains the changed constraints, records the replacement decision, and defines migration consequences.

best_practices: Capture concrete constraints and evidence before stating the decision.
Compare credible alternatives fairly and include negative consequences.
Create a superseding ADR instead of rewriting an accepted record.
anti_patterns: Do not document only the selected option without explaining alternatives.
Do not use vague decisions that lack ownership or measurable scope.
Do not treat an ADR as an implementation guide with excessive configuration detail.

faq.question: What is an Architecture Decision Record?
faq.answer: An ADR is a short document that records an important architecture choice, its context, alternatives, and consequences.

faq.question: Which ADR format does this skill use?
faq.answer: It follows the Nygard format with status, context, decision, consequences, alternatives, and optional references.

faq.question: Can this skill review an existing ADR?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply the included checklist to identify missing evidence, weak reasoning, operational concerns, and approval gaps.

faq.question: Does the skill choose the best architecture automatically?
faq.answer: No. It structures analysis and documentation, but the team remains responsible for evidence, trade-offs, and approval.

faq.question: How should an accepted ADR be changed?
faq.answer: Create a new ADR that supersedes the accepted record. Keep the original unchanged to preserve decision history.

faq.question: Can I adapt the templates for my organization?
faq.answer: Yes. Add relevant metadata, review roles, and governance steps while retaining clear context, decisions, alternatives, and consequences.
